Preface 


Presented herewith with pleasure is the first-ever English 
translation of the full text of the available version of Maliarshi 
Parasara’s Brihat Parasara Hora Sastra. But for the blessings 
of Lord Ganesa this would have been as uphill task forme.

Sri Maha Vishnu is the god f gods. So is ParasaraHora— 
the book of books in the field of astrology. 

The work is in the form of a carritch between sage Parasara 
and his disciple Maitreya who later himself became a worthy 
sage. Parasara belonging to Vasishta’s lineage was Veda Vyasa’s 
father. As could be seen in the course of progressing thorugh 
the text, sage Saunaka was the preceptor of Parasara in the 
inatter of astrology. Saunaka was one of the earliest sages and 

was Garga's disciple.

was Garga's disciple. 

The date of Parasara could be attributed to be roughly the 
efa of Dharma Raja of Maha Bharata. This can be understood 
when the sage states “in the present Yuga, Dharma Raja is bom 
with the combination of...” He further states that Salivahana 
'will be born with the same combination...’ Further, the reader 
could find statements relating to the horoscopic yogas of Maha 
Vishnu, Prajapati, Swayambhu Manu etc. which statement 
could possibly be made by no ordinary mortal.

Varaha Mihira in Brihat Sambita, Kalyana Varma in 
Saravali and many such other illustrious authors gave references 
Of Parasara’s astrological statements. 

Parasara Hora finds its translation in Bengali, Malayalam 
etc. which translations however have not been seen by me. I 
have with me the following versions.

Sri Venkateswata Press, Bombay, partly rendered in Hindi.

For a majority of slokas, one can find Sanskrit commentary only.

Hindi translation by Siiarara Jha. (Master Khelari Lai,
Varanasi edition)

Hindi translation by Devachandra Jha (Chaukambha
edition) 

4 . Hindi translation by Ganesa Datta Pathak (Thakur Prasad 
edition) 

After scrutinizing critically the four manuscripts, I have 
for reasona of more credibility chosen the Sanskrit version 
rendered by Sitararm Jha. The Chaukambha version is almost 
the same as that of Khclari Lai’s. 

Other versions that I have come across are :

Tamil translation by C. G. Rajan— for only 36 chapters,
without Sanskrit verses.

English translation by N. N. K. Rao for only 25 chapters,
without Sanskrit slokas. 

Thus, I have felt a need to make the original version 
available in English to the fullest possible extent. Our version 
has 97 chapters containing English translation and exhaustive 
annotations and examples. 

To handle the publication easily, we have divided the work 
in two volumes. The present Volume— first volume— contains 45 
chapters while the remaining 52 chapters have been put in the 
second volume.

Chapter 1 and chapter 2 give some preliminary extraastrological information. From chapter 3, the astrological 
information begins, ■ In this chapter, planetary descriptions, 
benefics and malefics, planetary deities, complexions, sex, 
primordial compounds, seasons, relationships, dignities etc- are 
given. Methods of calculating the 5 Upagrahas like Dhooma 
and Muhurta Velas like Gulika are given. These are totally ten 
and have their own say on a nativity, as the other nine main 
Grabas have. So to say, these Upagrahas and Muhurta velafc

Grabas have. So to say, these Upagrahas and Muhurta velafc 
can alter in suitable proportions the effects due to Nava Grahas. 




In the matter of calculation of Galika, a different concept comes 
to light from this oldest work. The later authors have given an 
altogether variable in knowing Gulika’s position whereas 
Parasara advised that it should be cast for the beginning of 
Saturn’s Muhurta. Whereas some suggest that it should be for 
the ending Muhurta of S3turn. 

In chapter 4, each Rasi is described from various angles. 
Slokas 25-30 are the climax of this chapter. An unerring

Slokas 25-30 are the climax of this chapter. An unerring 
method to find out the Nisheka Lagna (or the moment of 
fatercourse causing conception) from the time of birth is outlined. 
Though the process of calculation is as simple as a school 
student’s mathematical quiz, it has great truth in it which even 
modern science could not discover. To prove the truth of the 
statement in the sage’s instruction, a practical example has been 
given by me. An assumed example cannot better solve the

given by me. An assumed example cannot better solve the 
problem. A practical case where the time of coitus is astrologically chosen is taken in hand; time of birth has also been got 
accurately noted. From the time of birth, the time of Nisheka 
(or of coitus) is traced whieh is not in variation, even to the 
slightest extent, with the originally noted Nisheka time. Again 
from the time of Nisheka, the birth time is traced in a forward 
manner using only traditional rules of astrology. This exercise 
proves three important points, viz-

proves three important points, viz- 

1. The point of M.C. is to be found out in the natal horoscope and houses intersected accordingly. This is popularly 
called Sripati Paddhati- Originally Parasara advocated this 
system.

Gulika’s position should be found out for the beginning of
Saturn’s Muhurta only.

Lahiri’s Ayanamsa is the first best. The reader will find
that we have used Moon's exact longitude in the above 
process. Simple angular distance by any Ayanamsa will 
position will take us far away from the truth. With Lahjri’s 
Ayanamsa, we can safely work out even Nadiamsas, which 
change fast. 






The method given by me in working out the future birth 
time from the time of coition can very well help the astrologers 
to foretell the exact moment of birth from the time of query. 
Reseaches reveal that time of query has a perfect alignment with 
the time of Nisheka.

Chapter 5 touches various special Lagnas, like Ghatika 
Lagna, Hora Lagfla and Bhava Lagna. The importance of these 
ascendanss cannot be underestimated. A final Bhava chart can 
various special ascendaDts. This final bhava chart can only 
reveal the extent of planetary effects when considered housew.je 
whereas the bhava chart exclusively prepared on natal ascendant 
alone can sometimes mislead. This is what the sage emphasises 
In sloka 9. 

Cpme to chapter 6. The zodiac is divided in to sixteen 
Vargas or divisions. These are called Shodasa Vargas. How to

Vargas or divisions. These are called Shodasa Vargas. How to 
find out such Vargas and their use are fully explained. These 
are from Rasi down to Shashtiamsa. In the classification, the 
vargas are made in four groups, i,e. 6 vargas, 7 Vargas, 10 Vargas 
and 16 Vargas and special technical names have been given for 
the total number of desirable vargas a planet attained for easy 
identification. For example if a planet is said to be in Golokamsa, it indicates that out of 16 Vargas, it is in 15 good V igas. 
These technical names appear in the gradation of Raja Yogas.

These technical names appear in the gradation of Raja Yogas. 

Each Varga finds a certain specific use in preference to a 
planet’s Rasi position. For example, without considering the 
Dvadasamsa chart no tangible resuits due to the native’s parents 
can be known. In deciding one’s career, the Dasamsa positions 
of the planets are of supreme importance. These are highlighted 
in chapter 7. In this very chapter the sage enunciates what is 
of 20 points taking again differently the four Varga classifications, 
viz. Shadvarga, Sapta Varga, Dasa Varga and Shodasa Varga.

viz. Shadvarga, Sapta Varga, Dasa Varga and Shodasa Varga. 
The consideration here is whether a planet is placed in own sign, 
friendly sign, enemy’s sign and the like in the concerned Varga 
planet will be capable of revealing in a dasa. 




Chapter 8 deals with what is called Jaimini aspects on Rasi 
basis. Maharshi Jaimini was the sage who expanded these 
Parasari principles very extensively m Sutra form for easy 
memorization and successful applicability. The original concept 
is however from the pen of Parasara.

Childhood evils are discussed in chapter 9 whiie chapter 10 
prescribes planetary combinations to combat such possible evils. 

Basic information about the 12 houses could be found in 
chapter 11 while specific attention may be given to slokas 14-16. 
These 3 slokas serve an important key in knowing how a Bhava 
is going to give effects under various circumstances.

Chapters 12-23 give a variety of information and instructions in analysing the 12 houses of a horoscope in a systematic 
manner. A close study of these rules will tame one’s mind to 
scientifically approach the horoscope for fruitful resuts. 

Chapter '24 is again one of the most important chapters. 
Here, the various effects of a Bhava lord being in a specific house 
are given. All the 12 lords are fully covered. How to sort out 
a situation in case of contrary indications is given in slokas

The bhava effects of Dhooma, Vyatipata, Gulika etc., are 
narrated fully in chapter 25. Pranapada Lagna’s position vis-a- 
vis natal ascendant also reveals certain special effects as could be 
seen in this very chapter. 

Shadbala calculations, Ishta and Kashta phalas and other 
related mathematical aspects are elaborately laid down in the 3 
chapters, viz. 26, 27 and 28.

It is not in order if planets are studied with reference to 
mere natal chart. Padas for various houses will further alter the 
planetary effects. This is what is taught in chapter 29. Raja 
Yogas, inter alia are best analysed through Arudha chart or Pada 
chart. The sage suggests Graha Padas as well, but unfortunately he leaves it at that without adding much information.’ 

For still deeper research, Upapada will be more effective. 
This area will give more clues particularly about marriage, finance 
and diseases. See chapter 30.

Chapter 31 entitled ‘Argaladhyaya’ though brief has worthy 
information on planetary interventions, obstructions and effects 
thereof. 





Significance of planets is treated in chapter 32. 

Karakamsa is the Navamsa Rasi occupied by Atma 
Karaka. Plenets forming a certain relationship with Karakamsa 
and their effects are narrated in chapter 33 extending to 99 
slokas.

Chapter 34 is again one of the most instructive. Planets 
assume a certain tendency by virtue of owning a certain house. 
The sage elaborately touches such roles for various planets for 
all the 12 ascendants. He decides on such principles the Yoga 
Karakas, Voga Bhanga, Karakas and Marakas for each ascendant. 
This will enable us understand whether planet will give beneficial results or adverse effects. Death dealing planets or Mrakas 
allow us to guess the period of one’s death.

As the name implies, chapter 35 lists Nabhasa Yogas which 
are available In most standard texts. Many new Raja Yogas 
could be found in chapter 36, like Khadga, Mridanga, Chamara, 
Kahala etc. . 

Chapters 37 and 38 deal with Lunar and Solar yogas which 
are popularly known. Raja yogas in chapter 39, Yogas for 
royal association in chapter 40, and financial combinations in 
chapter 41 deserve "Special mention, containing a variety of 
authoritative information.

Maraka or death dealing planets bave a say on the finances 
of the native apart from causing his end. These are tersely 
enlightened in the 42nd chapter. 

The chapter on longevity, bearing No. 43, is among the 
most important ones. PindayU, Naisargayu, Amsayu and the 
like, and computations based on ascendant/planetary pairs 
linking with movable, fixed and common signs contain instructive information. In the notes, I have taken Pindayu calculations 
and worked out a fullfiedged example touching all aspects of 
computation. I have adopted a scientific method for deductions

computation. I have adopted a scientific method for deductions 
for planetary contributions arising by placement in bhavas 12 
to 7. I have simply not considered bhava positions 
in these deductions but degree-wise positions of the various 
planets. I have given one common formula covering the six 
bhavas and the reader can work out the exact loss of longevity. 
This can be usefully extened to any loss of years as far as 




bhavasl2to7 is concerned in other systems as well. Other 
longevity calculations have been suitably annotated by me.

The reader will also do well to study chapter 44 concerning 
Marakas before he takes a decision on longevity. Rahu/Ketu 
have also been assigned Marakatwa roles. 

The concluding chapter of Vol 1 is the 45th dealing with a 
number of kinds of Avasthas of the planets. Out of these, the 
12 Avasthas, known as Sayanadi Avasthas are of supreme importance. If one tries to interpret these Avasthas in proper spirit, 
he will be able to detect the diseases the native will suffer. I 
have supported my views with the help of information from

have supported my views with the help of information from 
Adbhuta Sagara of Ballala Sena and Hora Ratna of Balabhadra. 
For example, if Mars is in Agamanavastha, one will suffer from 
deep ear pains. , In the normal parlance, we consider only Jupiter 
in the context of ear defects. Diseases of hand and foot are 
assigned to Venus in Agamanavastha. If one conducts a scientific research in the matter of diseases with the help of planetary 
Avasthas, viz. Sayanadi Avasthas, one is bound to reach many 
brilliant clues.

Avasthas, viz. Sayanadi Avasthas, one is bound to reach many 
brilliant clues. 

The present work offers a vast scope for success in predictive astrology. One can build up his own applied astrology 
instead of theoretical astrology if he works on the lines suggested 
by Maharslii Parasara.

A word of caution is necessary for the benefit of the reader, 
In order to understand the hidden aspects of the various rules 
given herein, what is required is a thorough understanding of 
these principles. Skipping over fast to an ensuing chapter may 
not convey the real idea of a ‘present’ chapter. To make the 
reader’s Job easier, I have explained every difficult aspect as 
clearly as I understand based on my own experience and study of 
other authoritative texts,

In the end, I would like to mention that my attempt to 
translate this great work and annotate may not have been wholly 
successful. I surely would have left some shortcomings unnoticed and unrectified. From the readers, I can only expect the 
affection of forgiving me for any innocent lapses.

Offering his Pbeisance to all-knowing sage Parasaru
and with folded hands, Maitreya said, “O Venerable, Astrology, 
the supreme limb of the Vedas, has three divisions, viz. Hora, 




Brihat Porasara Hora Sastra 


Ganita and Samhita. Among the said three divisions, Hora or 
genethliac part of astrology is still more excellent, I desire to 
know of its glorious' aspects from you. Be pleased to tell me, 
“How this Universe is created ? How does it end ? What is the 
relationship of the animals born on this earth with the 
heavenly bodies ? Please speak elaborately”.

Notes : Maitreya was Parasara’s ardent disciple. Sage 
. Parasara was the illustrious father of Bhagawan Veda Vyasa. 
Parasara Smriti, Parasara Samhita and the present work Parasara Hora are some of the immortal contributions made by 
our sage.

Parasara’s preceptor was sage Saunaka, the reputed author 
of Rigveda Pratisakbya and other vedic compositions, from 
whom he took instructions in astrology. Saunaka was taught by 
Narada, son of Lord Brahma Pitamaha in the matter of astrology and others. Narada got direct instructions from Pitamaha. 
These details are stated by sage Parasara in the concluding 
cnapter of the present work. 

The sage predicts in the course of his treatise that Salivatuna will be born In a yoga caused by relationship between an 
angular lord and a trinal lor as both are in Simhasanamsa, vide

While the technicalities of the astrological
part of this statement will be understood by the reader as he 
progresses with the study of this work, it will be evident that 
Parasara was much before Salivahana. The era of Sallvahana 
commenced in AD 72. Since Veda Vyasa is reverentially referred 
as Parasaratmaja, meaning the offspring of Parasara, Sage Parasara lived during Maha Bbarata era.

Sage Maitreya’s name appears in Veda Vyasa’s Srimad 
Bhagavata Parana. Maitreya was sage Kusaru’s offspring. Sage 
Maitreya achieved a great deal of knowledge in spiritual and 
other topics. Vidura abandoned his kith and kin and met sage 
Maitreya to achieve religious merits. 

As can be seen, our text is in the form of a carritch 
between sage Parasara and Maitreya. the Master and the Disciple 
respectively. 

Astrology has three divisions, viz. Hora, Ganita and 
Samhita. Hora deals with genethliac part while mathematical

are like Rig Veda Samhita. Charaka Samhita, Vasishta Samhita 
etc. Thus Samhita is not an original work.

friendship on the other, Saturn becomes equal to Mars. Take 
again the relationship of Venus. He owns the 2nd and 7th from 
the Moolatrikona of Mars, thus becoming friend and enemy 
respectively. Hence he is neutral to Mars.

movable sign which will yield Paranapada. If the Sun is in a

indicates an inauspicious birth.

SIGN ASPECTS : O Maitreya, now detailed are the
aspects emanating from the signs Aries etc. Every movable 
sign aspects the 3 fixed signs leaving the fixed sign adjacent to 
it. Every fixed sign lends aspect to the 3 movable signs barring 
the adjacent movable sign. And a common sign aspects the 
other three common signs. The planet in a sign lends the same 
aspect as the sign (in which the planet is) does.

Notes : Apart from usual aspects of planets, Maharshi 
Parasara deals with Rasi aspects or sign aspects. These are also 
used by sage Jaimini fa discipie of Vedavyasa and author of 
Poorva Meemamsa etc.) and this system came to be known as 
Jaimini system though the original propounder is Parasara. 





Brifiat Parasara Hora Sastfa . 


Jaimini Maharshi is also an equally worshipped authority on 
astrology. He mainly uses Rasi aspects, Rasi Dasas apart from 
many other Dasas, Arudha Pada, Atma Karaka etc. by longitudes, Karakamsa etc.

The current 3 slokas throw light on the sign aspects. Each 
ipovable Rasi aspects 3 fixed signs, leaving the nearest fixed sign. 
For example, Aries — movable sign- — does not aspect Taurus but 
Leo, Scorpio and Aquarius. Taurus— a fixed sign aspects 

3 movable signs, viz. Cancer, Libra and Capricorn but does 
not aspect Aries, the nearest movable sign. Gemini’s aspects 
are on Virgo, Sagittarius and Pisces. The planet in assign 
aspects similar signs as above and also the occupant thereof. 
Hence, in these aspects, longitudes of the aspector and the 
aspected are ignorable.

Take for instance a birth on 15th February 1947 at 
Jodhpur 73 E 2 and 26 N 18. The local sun rise is at 0638 hrs 
and sun set at 1749 hrs. Hence for this latitude and date, 
the day duration is llh 11m and night duration 12h 49m, 
Divide the day duration by two to get Dinardha which indicates 
5h 35m. Similarly dividing night duration by 2 wc get Nisardha 
as 6h 24m. Add 5h 35m to Sun rise which will give half the 
day duration. Thus by adding 5h 35m to 6h 38m, we get

day duration. Thus by adding 5h 35m to 6h 38m, we get 
12h 13m. Similarly in the case of night, the night duration 
of 12h 49m be halved and the figure arrived at is to be added 
to sun set. Thus wcget Oh 13m (i.e. 13 m later than the 
usual mid-night). 

From the above we may understand that by simply taking 
12 noon as mid-day and 0 hour as mid-night it will not serve our 
purpose in the context of the yoga suggested by the sage. Needless to mention that LMT is to be used for these calculations.

Vimsottari Dasa

Beginning from Krittika the lords of Dasas

(1) Aries, Leo and Sagittarius, (2) Taurus, Virgo and Capritorn, (3) Gemini, Libra and Aquarius and (4) Cancer, Scorpio

Chapter 1: The Twelve Bhavas and Modern Predictive Judgment

The Second House (Dhana Bhava) governs movable wealth, earned income, family lineage, speech, and food intake. When occupied or aspected by benefics like Jupiter or Venus, the person speaks truth with elegance and accumulates steady wealth.

The Fourth House (Sukha Bhava) represents maternal happiness, inner peace, land, vehicles, real estate, and formal academic degrees. Malefics like Mars or Saturn here can create domestic friction or early separation from home, while fostering disciplined tenacity.

The Fifth House (Putra Bhava) governs intelligence (Buddhi), purva punya (past-life merit), creative genius, children, and speculative investments. Being the principal Dharma trine, planets placed here bestow natural intuitive wisdom and spiritual inclinations.

The Seventh House (Kalatra Bhava) indicates the marriage partner, legal partnerships, public dealings, and sexual passions. It is also an angle (Kendra) and a death-inflicting house (Maraka). Afflictions here delay marriage but often yield greater emotional maturity when union occurs.



Chapter 2: Planetary Nature and Modern Dasha Interpretation

Saturn (Shani) represents endurance, duty, delay, discipline, and karmic retribution. Rather than purely "evil", Hindu astrology views Saturn as the great stabilizer that burns away superficial delusions, giving lasting accomplishments through patient perseverance.

Rahu (the North Node) acts as an amplifying, worldly force of obsessive ambition, innovation, and foreign connections. Ketu (the South Node) acts as a spiritualizing, contracting force of liberation, detachment, and subtle psychic insight. Their dashas bring sudden, non-traditional turning points.

If the lord of an angle (Kendra) and the lord of a trine (Trikona) establish mutual reception, conjunction, or aspect, they become Yogakarakas, producing high auspiciousness, professional advancement, and fortune during their respective Vimshottari dasha periods.

Benefic planets (Jupiter, Venus, unafflicted Mercury, Waxing Moon) owning Kendra houses lose their natural beneficence and produce neutral or obstructive effects, whereas natural malefics (Saturn, Mars, Sun) owning Kendra houses shed their maleficence and act constructively.

The 6th, 8th, and 12th houses are Trik houses (dusthanas). Any bhava lord placed in these houses suffers depletion and obstacles regarding its primary significations, unless involved in a Viparita Raja Yoga.

When the lord of the 6th, 8th, or 12th house is positioned exclusively in another dusthana (6th, 8th, or 12th) without association or aspect of auspicious trine lords, it produces Viparita Raja Yoga (Harsha, Sarala, or Vimala), generating unexpected fortune arising from the adversity of competitors.

Chapter 2: Predictive Rules for Vimshottari Dasha Analysis

When the Antardasha lord is placed in a Kendra (1st, 4th, 7th, 10th) or Trikona (5th, 9th), or in the 11th house from the Mahadasha lord and shares natural or temporal friendship, the period produces exceptional professional elevation, happiness, and material success.

During the Mahadasha of a planet owning the 10th house (Karma Bhava), any Antardasha of a planet occupying the 10th or aspecting the 10th house will activate decisive career milestones, authority promotions, or occupational transformation.

The period of a Maraka lord (lord of the 2nd or 7th house) produces bodily vulnerability, physical strain, or heavy financial expenditures, especially when afflicted by natural malefics or transit Saturn.

If a planet is retrograde (Vakra) in the birth chart, its dasha induces introspection, repeated efforts in its designated significations, and non-linear or unconventional outcomes that manifest suddenly after initial delay.

Chapter 3: Systematic Rules for Transits (Gochara)
Transits (Gochara) must primarily be judged from the natal Moon sign (Chandra Lagna), as the Moon signifies the mind, physical constitution, and immediate experiential reality of the native.

Saturn transiting the 12th, 1st, and 2nd houses from the natal Moon constitutes Sade Sati (a seven-and-a-half-year cycle). The first phase affects expenses and foreign travels, the second phase tests personal health and identity, and the third phase disciplines family finances and speech.
Jupiter transiting the 2nd, 5th, 7th, 9th, or 11th house from the natal Moon produces benefic expansion, marriage, progeny, wisdom, and financial grace, mitigating several adverse natal dashas.

The Seven Chara Karakas of Jaimini. In the Jaimini system of Jyotisha, seven variable planetary significators (Chara Karakas) are determined based on the descending order of their longitudinal degrees, minutes, and seconds within their respective signs (excluding Rahu and Ketu in the standard 7-karaka scheme): (1) Atmakaraka (planet with highest degree) representing the soul, core vitality, and life lesson; (2) Amatyakaraka (second highest degree) representing the career, ministerial council, and profession; (3) Bhratrukaraka (third highest) representing siblings, mentors, and spiritual

(3) Bhratrukaraka (third highest) representing siblings, mentors, and spiritual guides; (4) Matrukaraka (fourth highest) representing mother, emotional foundation, and domestic shelter; (5) Putrakaraka (fifth highest) representing progeny, intellect, creativity, and disciples; (6) Gnatikaraka (sixth highest) representing adversaries, obstacles, illness, and competitive struggle; and (7) Darakaraka (seventh, lowest degree) representing the spouse, intimate partnerships, and trade relationships.

Amatyakaraka and Career Achievement. The Amatyakaraka (AmK) governs livelihood, professional advisors, and vocational success. If the Amatyakaraka is strongly placed in the 1st, 5th, 9th, 10th, or 11th houses from the Lagna or from the Arudha Lagna, the native attains eminent professional rank, trusted advisory positions to governments or leaders, and lasting financial stability. If the Atmakaraka and Amatyakaraka form a mutual Kendra, Trikona, or conjunction, a supreme Jaimini Raja Yoga is created, guaranteeing high executive standing.
Darakaraka and Relationship Dynamics. The Darakaraka (DK) represents the spouse and relational karma

. The Darakaraka (DK) represents the spouse and relational karma. The nature of the planet acting as Darakaraka describes the character, temperament, and appearance of the partner: Sun as DK indicates an authoritative, dignified partner; Moon as DK indicates an intuitive, emotional partner; Mars as DK indicates an energetic, courageous partner; Mercury as DK indicates an articulate, youthful partner; Jupiter as DK indicates a wise, virtuous, and spiritual partner; Venus as DK indicates an artistic, refined partner; and Saturn as DK indicates a mature, prudent, and persevering partner.

Karakamsa Lagna and Spiritual Evolution. The sign in the Navamsha (D9) chart occupied by the Atmakaraka is termed the Karakamsa. Analyzing the Karakamsa Lagna and the 12 houses counted from it reveals the soul's deepest spiritual inclination and innate intellectual talents. Benefics in the 12th house from the Karakamsa (especially Ketu) signify spiritual liberation (Moksha) and higher contemplative states. The 1st and 5th houses from the Karakamsa reveal natural creative genius and philosophical orientation.

Arudha Lagna (Pada Lagna) and Social Image. Arudha Lagna (AL) is calculated by counting how many houses the Lagna lord is removed from the Lagna, and projecting that same distance forward from the Lagna lord's position. The Arudha Lagna signifies the native's external reputation, social standing, material manifestation, and how the world perceives the native. Benefic planets (Jupiter, Venus, Mercury) placed in the 1st, 2nd, 4th, 5th, 7th, or 11th houses from the Arudha Lagna create immense prosperity, spotless public honor, and material success.

Upapada Lagna (UL) and Marital Longevity. Upapada Lagna (UL or Gaunapada) is the Arudha of the 12th house. It is the primary Jaimini indicator for marriage, the partner's family background, and the stability of marital life. If benefic planets occupy or aspect the Upapada Lagna and its 2nd house, the marriage is harmonious, long-lasting, and blessed with virtuous children. If the 2nd house from the Upapada is afflicted by malefic planets (Sun, Saturn, Rahu, Mars) or debilitated planets, it indicates friction in partnership requiring conscious patience, mutual respect, and dedicated Upayas.

Foundations of Jaimini Chara Dasha. Unlike Vimshottari Dasha which is based on Nakshatras and planetary periods, Jaimini Chara Dasha is a sign-based (Rashi) dasha system. The dasha periods are counted through the 12 zodiacal signs in regular (direct/Savya) or reverse (indirect/Apasavya) order depending on whether the starting sign is odd or even, and whether the 9th house from it is odd or even. The duration of each sign dasha (from 1 to 12 years) is determined by the distance of the sign's lord from that sign
. Chara Dasha accurately pinpoints major life events, relocations, career elevations, and marital timing by examining the transit of Karakas through the operating Dasha signs.

PHRENOLOGY CONNECTED WITH ASTRO-PALMISTRY 

The study of the shape, protuberances and mental vibrations of 
the skull of a native and the mental capacity and character they reveal is 
the structure of the brain is controlled by Mercury. From the ear at 90°, 
(see Fig. No.3) towards the eyebrows and head, mind is divided into 42 
divisions (see Fig No.l). This division of 90° separates forehead fan the 
mind. The first division is to the right side and the second is to the left side 
of the face (see Fig. No.2). Each of the 42 parts is connected with one or

of the face (see Fig. No.2). Each of the 42 parts is connected with one or 
the other planet (please refer to the table on page No.56). In some cases 
more than one planet have a dominant effect over the other planet. These 
42 divisions are also twelve houses of the natal chart (See Fig. No. 6).

The divisions of the brain are complete at the age of 7 years and it 
is presumed that the 7 mounts on the palm had made their place in the natal 
chart. At the age of 35 all the planets complete their first circulation. The 
structure of the mind is same on the left and right side (see Fig. No.5). The 
42 divisions are the 42 years duration of Rahu which controls the mental 
vibrations. It may be noted here that division no. 27 to 42 are the results of 
division no. 1-26 which are not given that much importance in the oceanic 
knowledge.

Normally the left side of the brain remain active. However, at the 
time of annual transit the right side comes out of its dormant state which

houses have fixed house Lord also. If a house is considered a building, 
the sign Lord owns the foundation. Fixed House Lord owns the building. 
The mutual relationship of Sign Lord and Fixed House Lord whether 
friendly or inimical determines the disposition of the house. In case of 
friendship, the benefic effect is supplemented. Other wise, in inimical 
relationship, malefic effect comes. On top of this, the disposition of a

relationship, malefic effect comes. On top of this, the disposition of a 
posited planet in a particular house also makes its effect. The net effect 
would be determined by propensity of a posited (transitting) planet with 
respect to Sign Lord and Fixed House Lord.

Jupiterian House: An airy house not facing North-South. A 
courtyard on one side of the house and not in the centre. A peepal tree 
or a place of worship either be in the house or in close proximity. 

Solar House: An East facing house meant to receive sunlight. 
Courtyard in middle, water source on right side near exit gate and fire 
place in courtyard. 

Lunar House: A well, pond, flowing water inside/adjoining or very 
near the house.

Venusian House: Opposite to Solar house. Entrance porch/entiy 
gate facing North-South having white plaster. Some part of house would 
be Kuchcha. 

Martian (positive) House: Mars moves along Sun, Jupiter and 
Moon are like sentry. A North-South house with entry gate Kuchha or 
pucca (cemented or uncemented). 

Martian (negative) House: A South facing house. Tree along 
with the house and shade of a tree falling on it. Sweetmeat shop or a 
furnace or funeral place nearby. Neighbours issueless, if not himself.

with broad leaves. Jupiterean devoid of lunar trees around. If such trees, 
are there it will make Mercury inimical. (Peepal- Jupiter, Banyan - JupiterMoon, Berry- Mercury)

West. Dark room on right side, after entry. So long as there is no light 
in this room, Saturn gives benefic effect. Possibily a big stone in the 
house and entry steps are made of old wood. Perhaps having pillars too.

Rahu House: A big covered earthen hole on right side while entering. 
Water exit at entry point of house. Opposite house is lying uninhabited 
or its owner is issueless. House roof has changed many a times. A 
furnace, source of smoke or dirty water pool in close proximity. 

Ketu House: A covered house with the in flow of dirty air. Ketu 

gives clues to windows and doors. May be open from its three sides. Not 

more than three sons/grandsons in the house. A two way path nearby/ 

a fallen house in neighbourhood or a place for dogs to roam about.

Inviolable Precautions (Savdhanis): Never harm dogs or allow animals to be mistreated near the house; Avoid sour curd at night. Creature & Animal Seva (Jeev Seva): Feed two-colored (black-and-white / kabra) dogs with bread smeared in butter.

Ketu (Ketu) in House 7 Upayas and Precautions. Household Remedy: Maintain mutual respect and fidelity with spouse; avoid unreasonable suspicion or withdrawal. Symbolic Action (Jal Pravah / Earth): Float 7 two-colored dry coconuts in flowing river on Tuesdays. Inviolable Precautions (Savdhanis): Never conduct marriage ceremonies without parental blessings; Avoid keeping broken pottery. Creature & Animal Seva (Jeev Seva): Feed street dogs and white cows with freshly baked rotis.

Ketu (Ketu) in House 8 Upayas and Precautions. Household Remedy: Wear a gold chain or gold wire around neck; keep a pet dog at home or care for community dogs. Symbolic Action (Jal Pravah / Earth): Donate a dual-colored blanket and black-white sesame seeds in a shrine on Tuesdays. Inviolable Precautions (Savdhanis): Never consume meat or alcohol in the bedroom; Avoid ignoring chronic urinary or knee complaints. Creature & Animal Seva (Jeev Seva): Feed two-colored street dogs with bread soaked in warm milk.

Ketu (Ketu) in House 9 Upayas and Precautions. Household Remedy: Serve spiritual preceptors and ascetics; apply saffron or sandalwood tilak on forehead daily. Symbolic Action (Jal Pravah / Earth): Float yellow lemons and sesame seeds into flowing river water. Inviolable Precautions (Savdhanis): Never insult ancestral traditions or sadhus; Avoid accepting free gold from holy men. Creature & Animal Seva (Jeev Seva): Feed fish in temple ponds with kneaded flour pellets.

Ketu (Ketu) in House 10 Upayas and Precautions. Household Remedy: Maintain high professional character; keep a small piece of silver in pocket during job interviews. Symbolic Action (Jal Pravah / Earth): Pour raw milk mixed with honey at the roots of a sacred tree. Inviolable Precautions (Savdhanis): Never take credit for subordinate's work; Avoid dark multi-patterned work attire. Creature & Animal Seva (Jeev Seva): Feed two-colored stray dogs with rotis smeared with butter.

Ketu (Ketu) in House 11 Upayas and Precautions. Household Remedy: Wear a solid gold ring on the index finger; cultivate sincere and selfless friendships. Symbolic Action (Jal Pravah / Earth): Donate black and white blankets or sesame seeds to an old-age home on Tuesdays. Inviolable Precautions (Savdhanis): Never deceive commercial partners or elder relatives; Avoid hoardings of unusable electronic junk. Creature & Animal Seva (Jeev Seva): Feed stray dogs and birds with sweet baked rotis.

Ketu (Ketu) in House 12 Upayas and Precautions. Household Remedy: Serve elderly ascetics, sadhus, and teachers; keep a small gold piece under the pillow. Symbolic Action (Jal Pravah / Earth): Donate black and white sesame seeds (til) in a holy shrine. Inviolable Precautions (Savdhanis): Never speak ill of spiritual preceptors; Do not ignore recurring joint or urinary symptoms. Creature & Animal Seva (Jeev Seva): Feed street dogs regularly with sweet bread.

Lal Kitab Pitri Rina (Ancestral Debt) Identification and Upayas. Pitri Rina is indicated when Jupiter is afflicted by Saturn, Rahu, or Mercury in Kendra houses, causing chronic illness across generations and lack of family lineage continuation. Classical Upaya: Collect an equal amount of money or yellow grams from every living blood relative (father, uncles, brothers, sisters, children) and with that joint sum perform a collective feast or donation of food and holy scripture at a revered ancient shrine.

Matri Rina (Mother Debt) and Stri Rina (Spouse Debt) Upayas. When Moon or Venus are severely afflicted in the 2nd, 7th, or 8th houses accompanied by Ketu or Mars, Matri Rina or Stri Rina manifests as mental agony, infertility, or sudden family ruin. For Matri Rina, collect silver coins from all blood relatives and immerse them collectively into a sacred holy river. For Stri Rina, feed one hundred cows with fresh green grass or donate white cows to deserving sanctuaries.

Pancha Mahapurusha Yogas Definition and Formation. When Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, or Saturn occupy a Kendra (1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th house) identical with their own sign or their exaltation sign, they produce five distinct royal combinations known as the Pancha Mahapurusha Yogas: Ruchaka is formed by Mars; Bhadra is formed by Mercury; Hamsa is formed by Jupiter; Malavya is formed by Venus; and Sasa is formed by Saturn. The person born under these combinations attains eminent stature, noble reputation, leadership, wealth, and virtuous character corresponding to the planet forming the yoga.

Hamsa and Malavya Yoga Specific Results. The person born under Hamsa Yoga (Jupiter in Kendra in Cancer, Sagittarius, or Pisces) possesses a majestic disposition, pious nature, mastery of sacred philosophy and jurisprudence, profound moral discernment, and universal reverence from rulers and society. The person born under Malavya Yoga (Venus in Kendra in Taurus, Libra, or Pisces) enjoys extraordinary grace, artistic elegance, luxurious conveyances, radiant spouse, mastery of fine arts, and a calm, generous disposition blessed with longevity and domestic felicity.

Sasa Yoga and Mahapurusha Dignity. The person born under Sasa Yoga (Saturn in Kendra in Libra, Capricorn, or Aquarius) commands authority over villages, institutions, or multitudes. Though serious, reserved, and austere, the native commands steadfast endurance, formidable organizing prowess, political acumen, and sovereign influence gained through persistent perseverance and mastery over labor and resources.

Gaja Kesari Yoga Formation and Auspicious Fruits. When Jupiter occupies a Kendra (1st, 4th, 7th, or 10th house) counted from the Moon, Gaja Kesari Yoga is produced. The native born in this yoga becomes illustrious, endowed with boundless wisdom, overcomes all rivals through dignified conduct, achieves lasting repute, builds lasting charitable institutions, and remains prosperous, virtuous, and respected throughout life.

Lunar Yogas: Sunapha, Anapha, and Dhurdhura. When planets other than the Sun, Rahu, and Ketu occupy the 2nd house from the Moon, Sunapha Yoga is generated, giving self-earned riches, administrative skill, and keen intellect. When planets occupy the 12th house from the Moon, Anapha Yoga is formed, endowing the native with generous character, physical health, and detachment from worldly anxiety

. When planets occupy both the 2nd and 12th houses from the Moon, Dhurdhura Yoga is formed, blessing the person with abundant wealth, trustworthy conveyances, loyal associates, and uninterrupted contentment.

Kemadruma Yoga and Its Classical Cancellations. When there are no planets in the 2nd and 12th houses from the Moon (excluding Sun and nodes), Kemadruma Yoga is formed, indicating periods of sorrow, isolation, and mental despondency. However, Kemadruma is completely cancelled (Kemadruma Bhanga) if planets occupy Kendras from the Lagna or from the Moon, or if the Moon is conjoined with a benefic planet or aspected by Jupiter. Upon cancellation, the native overcomes early hardships and attains royal fortune.

Amala Yoga and Auspicious Governance. If a spotless benefic planet (Jupiter, Venus, or Mercury) occupies the 10th house from the Lagna or from the Moon without malefic affliction, Amala Yoga is formed. The native enjoys spotless fame, commands clean professional authority, engages in philanthropic statecraft, remains pure in speech and action, and is honored by sovereigns throughout life.

Viparita Raja Yogas: Harsha, Sarala, and Vimala. When the lord of the 6th house is placed in the 6th, 8th, or 12th house, Harsha Yoga is formed, giving invincibility over rivals, radiant health, and unwavering courage. When the lord of the 8th house is placed in the 6th, 8th, or 12th house, Sarala Yoga is formed, giving longevity, fearlessness, sudden gains, and victory over trials. When the lord of the 12th house is placed in the 6th, 8th, or 12th house, Vimala Yoga is formed, giving noble character, wise financial accumulation, independence, and spiritual purity
. In all three Viparita Raja Yogas, adversity transforms into unexpected elevation provided these lords do not conjoin other Kendra or Trikona lords.

Neechabhanga Raja Yoga Rules. When a debilitated planet (Neecha) has its dispositor (lord of the debilitation sign) or its exaltation lord in a Kendra from the Lagna or from the Moon, Neechabhanga Raja Yoga is formed. The native, after initial struggle and humbleness, rises to the rank of an emperor or minister, wielding great executive power and enduring wealth.

Functional Nature of Kendras, Trikonas, and Dusthanas. The 1st, 4th, 7th, and 10th houses are Kendras (Vishnusthanas), representing the pillars of action, vitality, domestic happiness, partnerships, and public reputation. The 1st, 5th, and 9th houses are Trikonas (Lakshmisthanas), representing divine grace, intellect, past meritorious karma (Purva Punya), and destiny (Bhagya). The 6th, 8th, and 12th houses are Dusthanas (Trika houses), governing obstacles, debts, chronic ailments, longevity, transformational crises, and expenditure
. Benefic planets in Kendras and Trikonas elevate the native, while planets in Upachaya houses (3rd, 6th, 10th, and 11th) flourish through courage and time.

Rahu and Ketu in the 12 Bhavas. Rahu in 3rd, 6th, 10th, and 11th houses confers immense material conquest, unconventional breakthrough, political mastery, and destruction of all opposing forces. Rahu in the 1st or 7th house creates intense worldly ambitions and unconventional partnerships requiring psychological clarity. Ketu in the 12th house is the supreme signifier of Moksha (spiritual liberation), granting deep meditative detachment and release from rebirth. Ketu in the 3rd or 6th house gives occult valor, immunity against insidious deceit, and resolute spiritual endurance.

The Principle of Vedha (Obstruction in Transits). A planet transiting a favorable house from the natal Moon sign has its benefic fruits obstructed (Vedha) if another planet (except between Sun and Saturn, or Moon and Mercury) simultaneously transits the corresponding obstruction house. When Vedha occurs, the promised auspicious result is neutralized or delayed until the obstructing planet leaves the Vedha house.

Kalatra Bhava Definition and Natural Karakas of Marriage. The 7th house (Kalatra Bhava) governs marriage, conjugal happiness, the nature and physical disposition of the spouse, long-term partnerships, and public alliances. Venus (Shukra) is the natural significator (Karaka) of marriage, romance, and aesthetic harmony for all natives, while Jupiter (Guru) acts as the special protector of marital wisdom, progeny, and noble companionship

. When the 7th house, its lord, and Venus are well-placed in Kendras or Trikonas and associated with benefics, the native enjoys enduring marital bliss, a virtuous and loyal spouse, and prosperous partnerships.

Judgment of Spouse Character from the Navamsha (D9). To ascertain the true temperament, moral character, and spiritual compatibility of the spouse, the wise astrologer must carefully examine the Navamsha of the 7th house (the setting Navamsha) and the disposition of the 7th lord in the Navamsha chart (D9). If the 7th lord or setting Navamsha falls in a sign of Jupiter or Venus, the partner is highly virtuous, dignified, compassionate, and faithful. If it falls in a sign of Mercury, the partner is learned, witty, and clever in business
. If it falls in a sign of Mars or Saturn, the partner is austere, bold, intense, or disciplined, requiring mutual compromise and conscious cultivation of emotional harmony.

Mars and Saturn Influences on the 7th House (Conscious Harmonization). The placement of Mars in the 1st, 4th, 7th, 8th, or 12th house (termed Kuja or Manglik influence) does not denote fatal destruction; rather, it indicates an abundance of fiery vitality, assertiveness, and emotional intensity that must be channeled into productive endeavors and shared physical activities. When harmonized through mutual understanding, spiritual maturity, or matching vitality in the partner's chart, this placement provides unwavering loyalty and courageous defense of the family
. Similarly, Saturn's aspect or occupation in the 7th delays marriage until personal maturity is attained, cementing an unbreakable, enduring foundation after initial trials.

Auspicious Yogas for Conjugal Harmony. When the lord of the Lagna and the lord of the 7th house are in mutual friendly signs, in mutual Kendras or Trikonas, or cast benefic aspects upon each other, deep mutual affection, lifelong fidelity, and harmonious cooperation prevail between the spouses. If the 2nd house (family), 4th house (domestic peace), and 7th house (partnership) are free from malefic affliction and guarded by Jupiter or Venus, domestic peace and prosperity flourish uninterrupted.

Timing of Marriage via Vimshottari Dasha and Gochara Transits. The sacred time of marriage manifests when the native operates the Vimshottari Mahadasha, Antardasha, or Pratyantardasha of: (1) the lord of the 7th house, (2) the lord of the Lagna, (3) natural Karaka Venus, (4) planets placed in or aspecting the 7th house, or (5) the dispositor of the 7th lord in the Navamsha

. Simultaneously, astronomical transit (Gochara) triggers must align: Jupiter transiting through or aspecting the 7th house from the Lagna or Moon, or transiting over the natal 7th lord or natal Venus, activates the divine window of matrimonial union and fruitful partnership.

Karma Bhava Definition and Scope of Professional Destiny. The 10th house (Karma Bhava) is the highest zenith of the sky (Madhya Lagna), governing profession, executive authority, public reputation, worldly status, leadership, and righteous vocation. The 10th lord, its placement, and the planets occupying the 10th house determine how the native manifests their divine purpose (Swadharma) and attains honor in society. An unblemished 10th house blesses the native with clean authority, social respect, and enduring legacy.

Benefics in the 10th House (Intellectual and Ethical Careers). Jupiter in the 10th house produces esteemed judges, ministers, preceptors, financial authorities, and noble philosophers who guide institutions with moral integrity. Mercury in the 10th confers renown in commerce, communications, literature, analysis, and diplomacy. Venus in the 10th elevates artists, designers, diplomats, and hospitality leaders, bringing wealth through creative arts and gracious public relations.

Saturn and Rahu in the 10th House (Mass Leadership and Resilience). Saturn in the 10th house raises the native through steady, dedicated toil, making them an indispensable organizer, industrial manager, or leader of the working populace. Though early career requires patience and discipline, Saturn bestows immense, enduring authority in the second half of life. Rahu in the 10th house gives extraordinary ambition, unconventional breakthroughs, foreign assignments, and rapid ascent in modern technological or political arenas.

Timing of Professional Advancement and Career Milestones. Professional elevation, promotions, and auspicious career transitions materialize during the operational periods (Mahadasha, Antardasha, or Pratyantardasha) of: (1) the 10th house lord, (2) planets occupying the 10th house, (3) the 6th lord (service, daily employment, and triumph over rivals), (4) the 11th lord (gains and promotions), or (5) the 2nd lord (accumulated wealth)
. When Jupiter or Saturn in Gochara transit casts an auspicious aspect on the 10th house or natal 10th lord, substantial professional recognition and occupational consolidation take place.

Sun in Gemini (Mithuna) and Cancer (Karka). Sun in Gemini makes the native learned, scholarly, wealthy, proficient in grammar, astrology, literature, and diplomatic discourse, with a pleasant and adaptable demeanor. Sun in Cancer makes the native emotionally sensitive, fond of ancestral homesteads, deeply attached to family, enduring in physical labor, and given to changes of residence.

Sun in Libra (Tula) and Scorpio (Vrischika). Sun debilitated in Libra makes the native face initial struggles with self-confidence, authoritative superiors, and balance of partnerships, requiring conscious cultivation of self-worth and legal prudence. Sun in Scorpio makes the native secretive, bold, formidable in research or military strategy, persistent in challenges, and possessing fiery willpower.

Sun in Sagittarius (Dhanus) and Capricorn (Makara). Sun in Sagittarius makes the native pious, revered by scholars and preceptors, rich in moral wisdom, philosophical, a counselor to leaders, and honorable in public life. Sun in Capricorn makes the native industrious, persevering through early obstacles, prudent in financial savings, quiet, and achieving steady success through disciplined craftsmanship.

Sun in Aquarius (Kumbha) and Pisces (Meena). Sun in Aquarius makes the native engaged in collective social movements, philosophical, detached from superficial vanities, and persevering in long-term goals. Sun in Pisces makes the native compassionate, fond of holy shrines, blessed with pearl and marine trade, prosperous through maternal or spiritual endowments, and possessing peaceful speech.

Moon in Aries (Mesha) and Taurus (Vrishabha). Moon in Aries gives swift movement, pioneering enthusiasm, round eyes, courageous temperament, and independence of spirit. Moon exalted in Taurus gives extraordinary physical grace, sweet voice, love of luxury and fine foods, unwavering emotional stability, enduring wealth, and affectionate fidelity.

Moon in Gemini (Mithuna) and Cancer (Karka). Moon in Gemini produces poetic wit, eloquence, skill in commerce and languages, charming humor, and intellectual curiosity. Moon in own sign Cancer gives tender maternal affection, deep intuition, agricultural and real estate wealth, popularity among friends, and emotional responsiveness.

Moon in Leo (Simha) and Virgo (Kanya). Moon in Leo gives noble carriage, magnanimous heart, dislike of subordination, courageous pride, and fondness for open nature and honors. Moon in Virgo gives modesty, analytical mind, mastery of music, arts, and scriptures, gentle manners, and financial precision.

Moon in Libra (Tula) and Scorpio (Vrischika). Moon in Libra gives refined aesthetic taste, graceful partnerships, diplomacy, and love of fair justice and trade. Moon debilitated in Scorpio gives intense, brooding emotions, deep occult insight, secretive determination, and transformational emotional depth requiring calm mindfulness.

Moon in Sagittarius (Dhanus) and Capricorn (Makara). Moon in Sagittarius gives religious devotion, upright moral character, generous hospitality, mastery of philosophy, and broad vision. Moon in Capricorn gives cautious practicality, organizational endurance, emotional resilience under austerity, and steady climb to authority.

Moon in Aquarius (Kumbha) and Pisces (Meena). Moon in Aquarius gives humanitarian idealism, intuitive grasp of social psychology, independence, and meditative vision. Moon in Pisces gives profound spiritual intuition, love of sacred waters, artistic genius, compassionate heart, and peaceful disposition.

Conjunction of Sun and Mercury (Budhaditya Yoga). When the Sun and Mercury are conjoined in a single house, Budhaditya Yoga is formed. The native becomes highly intelligent, eloquent, renowned for scholarship, skilled in administrative advisory roles, respected by sovereigns, and blessed with enduring learning and mathematical acumen.

Conjunction of Sun and Jupiter (Surya-Guru Yoga). When the Sun and Jupiter are conjoined, the native is deeply righteous, devoted to spiritual teachers, endowed with lofty moral stature, a trusted advisor to ministers or kings, wealthy, truthful, and blessed with spotless reputation.

Conjunction of Moon and Jupiter (Gaja Kesari Conjunction). When the Moon and Jupiter unite in one house, the person attains radiant fame, profound ethical judgment, immense wealth, universal affection, and noble leadership in education, state, or spiritual institutions.

Conjunction of Mars and Venus (Mangal-Shukra Yoga). When Mars and Venus are conjoined, the native is passionately artistic, attractive to the opposite sex, fond of luxurious ornament, passionate in romance, skilled in performance, and requiring mindfulness in marital commitments.

Conjunction of Jupiter and Saturn (Guru-Shani Yoga). When Jupiter and Saturn unite, the native possesses deep philosophical maturity, institutional vision, enduring patience, mastery of law and ancient traditions, and authority over large organizations and public works.

Foundations of Raja Yogas in Saravali. Raja Yogas (combinations for executive power and sovereignty) arise primarily when the lords of the Kendra houses (1st, 4th, 7th, 10th) form mutual relationships, conjunctions, or aspects with the lords of the Trikona houses (1st, 5th, 9th). The union of the 9th lord (fortune/dharma) and the 10th lord (action/karma) forms the supreme Dharma-Karmadhipati Raja Yoga, elevating the native to highest authority and noble fame.

Raja Yogas Formed by Benefics in Kendras. When all Kendra houses are occupied solely by natural benefics (Jupiter, Venus, Mercury, and waxing Moon) without malefic association, the native is elevated to the rank of a ruler or leader of men, blessed with longevity, prosperity, and unblemished honor.

Nabhasa Yogas: Ashraya and Dala Yogas. Nabhasa Yogas operate throughout life without being confined to particular dasha periods. The Ashraya Yogas depend on the signs occupied: Rajju (planets in movable signs) gives fondness for travel and ambition; Musala (planets in fixed signs) gives steadfast determination, immovable wealth, and unwavering purpose; Nala (planets in dual signs) gives adaptable ingenuity and intellectual flexibility.

Kalatra Bhava and Characteristics of the Spouse. According to Kalyanavarma in Saravali, the nature, beauty, and temperament of the spouse are discerned from the sign falling on the 7th house, its ruling planet, and the planets aspecting it. If the 7th house is ruled by Venus or Jupiter, the spouse is graceful, virtuous, endowed with modesty, sweet-spoken, and born of an honorable family. If ruled by Mercury, the spouse is intelligent, witty, skilled in business, and youthful. If ruled by Mars or the Sun, the partner is bold, energetic, commanding, and possesses high self-respect
. If ruled by Saturn, the partner is steadfast, quiet, serious, and deeply devoted to duties.

Planetary Conjunctions Influencing Conjugal Happiness. When natural benefics cast their full aspects on the 7th house and Venus is situated in an auspicious Rashi and Navamsha, the marriage is blessed with lifelong joy, mutual respect, and prosperity. If malefic planets aspect the 7th house, the couple must cultivate conscious patience, communication, and emotional self-discipline to transcend differences in temperament and forge a resilient, harmonious bond.

Professional Synthesis from the Lagna and the Moon. To evaluate livelihood and occupation accurately, examine the 10th house counted both from the Lagna and from the Janma Rashi (Moon sign). The stronger of the two houses, along with its lord and Navamsha dispositor, reveals the native's true vocational aptitude, whether in leadership, statecraft, commerce, arts, sciences, or engineering.

Planetary Significations of Rahu and Ketu. Rahu governs sudden fortunes, unconventional sciences, foreign languages, electronics, agate (gomedha), aviation, deceptive maneuvers, ancestral paternal lineage, and material ambition. Ketu governs spiritual enlightenment (Moksha), cat's eye gemstone, renunciation, divine insight, mathematical intuition, maternal ancestral lineage, surgery, astrology, and release from rebirth.

Rahu and Ketu as Powerful Yogakarakas. If Rahu or Ketu occupy a Kendra (1st, 4th, 7th, 10th) and are conjoined with or aspected by the lord of a Trikona (5th or 9th), or if they occupy a Trikona and are conjoined with or aspected by the lord of a Kendra, they become powerful Yogakarakas. During their Mahadashas and Antardashas, they confer immense political authority, royal wealth, vehicles, and renown surpassing even natural benefics.

Principles of Maraka and Longevity in Uttara Kalamrita. The 8th house and the 3rd house are the primary houses of longevity (Ayus). The 12th houses from them—namely the 7th house and the 2nd house—are designated as Maraka houses (houses causing termination of vitality or physical distress). The lords of the 2nd and 7th houses, along with planets placed in them or aspecting them, become Marakas

. However, when Maraka dashas operate, fear is unwarranted; the classical remedy is chanting the Maha Mrityunjaya mantra, performing Rudrabhisheka, giving food in charity (Annadāna), and dedicating oneself to righteous conduct, which converts physical fatigue into spiritual purification.
# Vedic Classical Predictive Rules & Aphorisms

Sun in the 1st House (Tanu Bhava). The native possesses high vitality, natural dignity, and authoritative demeanor. If Sun is exalted in Aries or in own sign Leo, the person attains executive authority, political prominence, and robust health. If debilitated in Libra or afflicted by Saturn or Rahu, eye weakness, cardiac sensitivity, and excessive ego-conflict may arise.

Sun in the 2nd House (Dhana Bhava). The native speaks with authority and firm conviction. Wealth is acquired through governmental, administrative, or family inheritance. If afflicted, harsh speech, dental or right-eye ailments, and dispute over ancestral property may occur.

Sun in the 4th House (Sukha Bhava). Creates interest in real estate, vehicles, and ancestral heritage, but can cause emotional restlessness or distance from the mother. The native possesses an honorable family background and deep philosophical inner conviction.

Sun in the 5th House (Putra Bhava). Bestows sharp intellect, creative brilliance, political acumen, and mastery over mantras. Children are honorable and ambitious. If afflicted, delay in progeny or friction with offspring may occur, but intellectual scholarship is prominent.

Sun in the 6th House (Shatru Bhava). Highly auspicious Upachaya placement. The native vanquishes all competitors, debts, and litigation. Immense physical resilience, capacity for hard work, and victory in competitive examinations or administrative service.

Sun in the 7th House (Kalatra Bhava). The spouse is proud, honorable, and from an influential family. Marital dynamics require conscious ego-management and mutual respect. Public partnerships and diplomacy are highlighted.

Sun in the 8th House (Randhra Bhava). Bestows deep interest in occult sciences, research, metaphysics, and unearned wealth or insurance. Health requires vital energy conservation, avoidance of harsh sunlight, and regular cardiac wellness practices.

Sun in the 9th House (Dharma Bhava). Supreme placement for spiritual destiny, righteousness, higher philosophy, and grace. The native respects the father, gurus, and moral codes. Pilgrimages, foreign travel, and fortunate life milestones are assured.

Sun in the 11th House (Labha Bhava). Excellent Upachaya placement for continuous income, influential professional networks, and fulfillment of long-term ambitions. Friends are wealthy and prominent. Wealth accumulates steadily.

Sun in the 12th House (Vyaya Bhava). Bestows foreign residence, spiritual inclination, meditative seclusion, and philanthropic expenditures. If well-placed, success in overseas institutions or hospitals; if afflicted, financial leakage and eye sensitivity.

Moon in the 1st House (Tanu Bhava). The native is magnetic, gentle, imaginative, emotionally responsive, and popular with the public. If Waxing Moon (Shukla Paksha), longevity, physical grace, and emotional balance flourish. If afflicted or dark Moon, mood fluctuations occur.
Moon in the 2nd House (Dhana Bhava). Bestows melodious, sweet speech, radiant facial beauty, family prosperity, and steady accumulation of liquid wealth and luxury assets.

Moon in the 4th House (Sukha Bhava). High Digbala placement. Bestows profound emotional peace, domestic bliss, maternal affection, fine vehicles, and luxurious home environments near water or gardens.

Moon in the 5th House (Putra Bhava). Sharp intuitive intelligence, speculative fortune, romantic nature, and meritorious, devoted children. High artistic creativity, counseling wisdom, and refined aesthetic taste.

Moon in the 7th House (Kalatra Bhava). The spouse is beautiful, affectionate, emotionally supportive, and devoted. Public relations, trade, partnerships, and commerce flourish through interpersonal charm.

Moon in the 8th House (Randhra Bhava). Deep psychological intuition, occult perception, and mystical insight. Emotional vulnerability requires meditative centering; inherited gains and research abilities are pronounced.
Moon in the 9th House (Dharma Bhava). Highly auspicious. Endows the native with religious devotion, divine grace, benevolent father, fortune through sea journeys, and respected philosophical stature.

Moon in the 10th House (Karma Bhava). Popular public figure, respected professional leader, flourishing in hospitality, psychology, public relations, commerce, or government service. Public esteem is high and enduring.

Moon in the 11th House (Labha Bhava). Abundant gains, influential female patrons, broad social circle, and realization of desires. Generates continuous prosperity and emotional fulfillment through community networks.
Moon in the 12th House (Vyaya Bhava). Solitary contemplation, foreign travels, spiritual liberation (Moksha), vivid dream consciousness, and philanthropic generosity.

Mars in the 1st House (Tanu Bhava). Bestows dynamic energy, athletic prowess, leadership, courage, and pioneering initiative. Creates Mangala/Kuja Dosha; marital partnerships require maturity and emotional temperance.

Mars in the 7th House (Kalatra Bhava). Dynamic, energetic, independent spouse. Kuja Dosha requires balanced partner matching or maturity past age 28; success in collaborative trade and assertive negotiation.

Jupiter in the 1st House (Tanu Bhava). Attains supreme Digbala. Blesses the native with wisdom, noble character, commanding presence, divine protection, and scholarly reputation. Casts auspicious 5th, 7th, and 9th Drishti on houses of children, marriage, and fortune.
Jupiter in the 5th House (Putra Bhava). Extraordinary intelligence, past-life merit (Purva Punya), profound scholarship in law, philosophy, or astrology, and brilliant, virtuous children.
Jupiter in the 7th House (Kalatra Bhava). Blesses the native with an educated, morally upright, noble, and prosperous spouse. Guarantees harmonious marriage, business integrity, and societal honor.

Jupiter in the 9th House (Dharma Bhava). Most sacred placement. The native is righteous, deeply blessed by Guru and providence, prosperous, and devoted to truth. Fortune rises naturally without friction.
Jupiter in the 11th House (Labha Bhava). Tremendous accumulation of righteous wealth, visionary elder friends, charitable gains, and complete fulfillment of noble life aspirations.

Saturn in the 10th House (Karma Bhava). Monumental rise through patient toil, administrative discipline, and perseverance. Governs public institutions, industry, law, politics, or management. Fall from grace occurs only if hubris or corruption enters; ethical vigilance preserves towering success.

Rahu in the 10th House (Karma Bhava). Phenomenal unconventional career rise, technological innovation, political power, mass media prominence, and foreign engagement. Breaks traditional boundaries to achieve unconventional authority.
Ketu in the 12th House (Vyaya Bhava). The ultimate classical placement for spiritual emancipation (Moksha), detachment from worldly vanity, psychic perception, and profound enlightenment.

Lord of the 10th House in the 1st House. The native is self-made, independent, and forges their own professional destiny. Career becomes intrinsic to their personality; public standing and personal honor are indivisible.
Lord of the 10th House in the 11th House. Immense financial gains through profession, influential professional alliances, commercial expansion, and fulfillment of career aspirations.
Lord of the 7th House in the 7th House. Blesses with a charming, devoted spouse, marital longevity, prosperous partnerships, and excellent diplomatic abilities.
Lord of the 7th House in the 1st House. The spouse is deeply devoted to the native; marriage significantly enhances personal status, vitality, and social confidence.

Lord of the 9th House in the 10th House (Dharma-Karmadhipati Yoga). Highest classical Raja Yoga. Divine fortune and righteous action unite, conferring supreme fame, royal or government honor, and lasting societal legacy.
Lord of the 9th House in the 9th House. Absolute divine grace, righteous prosperity, celebrated paternal lineage, spiritual elevation, and continuous good fortune.

Gaja Kesari Yoga. Formed when Jupiter is in a Kendra (1st, 4th, 7th, 10th) from the Moon. The native is illustrious, highly educated, virtuous, respected by rulers, endowed with lasting reputation, and capable of overcoming all adversaries.

Budhaditya Yoga. Formed by the conjunction of Sun and Mercury in a favorable house. Conveys sharp analytical intellect, oratorical skill, mathematical ability, administrative brilliance, and professional prestige.

Pancha Mahapurusha Yogas. Mars in Kendra in own/exaltation forms Ruchaka (fearless valor); Mercury forms Bhadra (intellectual genius); Jupiter forms Hamsa (saintly wisdom); Venus forms Malavya (artistic luxury); Saturn forms Sasa (commanding authority over institutions).

Neechabhanga Raja Yoga. Formed when a debilitated planet's dispositor or exaltation lord occupies a Kendra from Lagna or Moon. Transformative reversal: early struggles turn into spectacular success and supreme distinction.

Viparita Raja Yogas. Lords of Dusthanas (6th, 8th, 12th) occupying only Dusthana houses form Harsha, Sarala, or Vimala yogas. The native achieves unexpected triumph out of adverse circumstances and vanquishes rivals.

Pratyantardasha Micro-Timing. Breakthrough events (job offers, marriage dates, financial windfalls) crystallize when the Pratyantardasha lord aligns with the primary significators of the natal promise and receives supportive Gochara transit aspects.

Saturn Sade Sati Classical Timing. Occurs when transit Saturn moves through the 12th, 1st, and 2nd houses from the natal Moon (approx. 7.5 years). Demands humility, discipline, restructuring, and elimination of complacency. Does not cause ruin; rewards patient, ethical effort and penalizes shortcuts.
